newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks soften at open, watching U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks soften at open, watching U.S..

text.p: The Australian share market softened at the open on Friday with modest losses among the leaders as traders moved to the sidelines ahead of U.S. inflation figures due later on Friday.
The All Ordinaries index dipped 6.3 points to 2,386.6.
Traders said the market had offered few surprises so far with the mild weakness on Wall Street and hesitation ahead of U.S. producer price index tempering local interest.

"People are a little nervous ahead of the U.S. inflation figures tonight," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage, noting that Wall Street's reaction to the figures was likely to lead proceedings next week.
"It will probably set the tone for next week."

Victorian-based regional Bank of Melbourne dived sharply, down 21 cents to an intraday low of A$9.25 (US$7.31), as investors fretted over the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's attitude to Westpac Banking Corporation's A$9.75 per share bid. Westpac shares were four cents lower at A$6.62.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
